Who Leads the Forbes 2026 Billionaire Ranking?
Elon Musk ranks first in the Forbes 2026 annual billionaire list with an estimated net worth of $839 billion, followed by Larry Page at $257 billion and Sergey Brin at $237 billion. Forbes used stock prices and exchange rates from March 1, 2026 for this annual ranking.
This page ranks the first 100 people in that fixed Forbes annual snapshot by estimated net worth in U.S. dollars. The numeric ranking uses one primary source: the Forbes 2026 World’s Billionaires annual list. Forbes Real-Time and Bloomberg are supplementary methodology references and are not used to replace the annual-list values.
Coverage: 100 people. Unit: USD billions at the March 1, 2026 valuation snapshot. Direction: higher estimated net worth ranks higher. Status counts: 100 published industry estimates; 0 official values; 0 calculated values; 0 official forecasts; 0 modeled projections.

What This Richest-People Ranking Measures
The ranking compares estimated personal net worth rather than income, salary, company revenue or cash holdings. Forbes estimates wealth using public-company stakes, private businesses and other identifiable assets under its valuation methodology.
Using one annual valuation date makes the 100 entries directly comparable within this dataset. Live wealth trackers can show different figures later as share prices, exchange rates, transactions and private-company valuations change.

The 50 Richest People in the World (October 2026)
By Cody Reynolds
Last updated October 15, 2026 · 6 min read
The 50 richest people in the world are worth a combined $5.96 trillion , according to Forbes real-time estimates as of October 2, 2026 . Elon Musk leads with about $919 billion, more than double the $368 billion of Jeff Bezos in second place. The ten richest alone hold just over $3 trillion, slightly more than the other 40 on this list combined.
Below is the full top 50 ranking, followed by what stands out in the data, how these fortunes are estimated, and why the numbers move so much from week to week. For individual profiles, see our celebrity net worth hub and the richest business people rankings.
Key takeaways
Elon Musk is still No. 1 , with an estimated $919 billion from his stakes in Tesla and SpaceX, up from $839 billion on Forbes’ annual list in March 2026.
Technology dominates: 13 of the 50 made their fortunes in tech, including all nine of the top nine.
The United States accounts for half the list (25 of 50), followed by China and Italy with three each.
19 people are worth $100 billion or more (the “centibillionaires”).
Seven women make the top 50, most of them heirs to family companies such as Walmart, L’Oréal, Koch, Mars and MSC. Abigail Johnson of Fidelity runs her family’s company as CEO.
Top 10 richest people in the world
Elon Musk — $919 billion (Tesla, SpaceX)
Jeff Bezos — $368 billion (Amazon)
Larry Page — $278 billion (Google)
Michael Dell — $266 billion (Dell Technologies)
Sergey Brin — $256 billion (Google)
Mark Zuckerberg — $249 billion (Meta)
Jensen Huang — $200 billion (Nvidia)
Larry Ellison — $179 billion (Oracle)
Steve Ballmer — $159 billion (Microsoft)
Warren Buffett — $142 billion (Berkshire Hathaway)
Net worth is in U.S. dollars, rounded to the nearest billion. Figures are Forbes real-time estimates as of October 2, 2026. Family fortunes are listed under the person Forbes ranks.
